turns.text: real quick need help planning thanksgiving groceries. its at my moms duplex and im bringing mac and cheese. want to make a baked one w 3 cheeses. how much of everything do i buy

Happy to help! A few quick questions so the amounts fit: how many people are you feeding, and what's your budget for the whole grocery run? For a baked three-cheese mac, a good rule is about 1 lb of dry pasta per 6-8 people as a side.

A starter version for a 9x13 pan (roughly 8-10 servings):
- 1 lb elbow macaroni
- 8 oz sharp cheddar
- 8 oz Gruyere or Monterey Jack
- 4 oz Parmesan or Colby for the top/blend
- 3 tbsp butter, 3 tbsp flour, 3 cups whole milk
- Breadcrumbs, salt, pepper, mustard powder, paprika

Tell me headcount and budget and I'll scale it.
like 8 people. also im dropping off sides and canned goods for her before the day so need a list for that too. budget around 120 total

8 people fits that recipe well. Here's a plan within $120:

Mac and cheese (~$22)
- Pasta, 3 cheeses, butter, flour, milk, breadcrumbs, spices

Sides and canned goods (~$75)
- Canned green beans x3 (or frozen)
- Canned corn x2
- Cranberry sauce x2
- Chicken or turkey broth x2 cartons
- Canned yams or 3 lb sweet potatoes
- Stuffing mix x2
- Gravy packets or jars x2
- Potatoes, 5 lb bag
- Rolls
- Canned pumpkin and a pie crust

Cushion (~$23) for anything that runs high.

Should I adjust for what your mom already has?

ok. ridgeline pays every other friday so ill shop after the next payday. and i already send her 250 every other friday for her electric bill. the mom fund. should groceries come out of that or my own cash

I'd keep them separate. The $250 is already earmarked for her electric bill, so if groceries come out of it, that bill could end up short. Use your own cash for the groceries and treat the $120 as its own line in your budget.

Since you get paid every other Friday, a simple setup:
- Payday: send the $250 first, then set aside $120 for groceries.
- Shop that weekend, a few days ahead of the holiday, so canned goods can be dropped off early and the cheese stays fresh.
- Buy the milk and cheese last, close to the day you bake.

If the $120 feels tight after the transfer, trim the cushion or buy store-brand canned goods and you'd land closer to $95.
lol ok that helped. short version of the list pls

Short version:

Drop-off (cans/sides): green beans x3, corn x2, cranberry sauce x2, broth x2, yams, stuffing x2, gravy x2, potatoes 5 lb, rolls, pumpkin + pie crust.

Mac: 1 lb elbows, 8 oz sharp cheddar, 8 oz Gruyere or Jack, 4 oz Parmesan, butter, flour, 3 cups milk, breadcrumbs, spices.

Budget: $120 from your own cash, separate from the $250.
